items.title: The pullback of a sheaf along the projection of the qc site of locally quasi-compact spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the sheaf (f : Y -> X) maps to Gamma(Y, f^{-1}F) on the qc site of locally quasi-compact spaces as the pullback of F along the projections to the Zariski and qc topologies (statement lines 7674-7686). The proof has three genuinely different parts. The Zar-sheaf property is immediate (proof lines 7689-7693), but the qc-sheaf property is not: by the sheaf criterion one must prove injectivity, which uses surjectivity of qc coverings and detection of equality at stalks, and then gluing after refinement via the plus construction (proof lines 7696-7711). The gluing itself requires two steps, first manufacturing a compatible family of stalk values from local sections over opens W_i of the base (proof lines 7713-7732) and then showing that family is a global section by covering a neighbourhood of an arbitrary point with finitely many quasi-compact pieces and shrinking until finitely many local sections agree (proof lines 7734-7745). Finally the identification with the pullbacks follows by comparing with the explicit colimit description of the pullback and its sheafification (proof lines 7747-7760). The claim is H2: three separate arguments, of which the second is a real topological gluing argument.
